column2: Alteration Lead missing from Acuity sync (Zoia Kozakov)
column3: A client’s record shows no Alteration Lead in Airtable even though Acuity shows “RR” (Rosa Rodriguez). Julia asked whether edits in Airtable feed back to Acuity or vice versa.
column10: The Acuity data was never actually missing — both of Zoia Kozakov's alterations appointments have Rosa Rodriguez correctly set as the Alterations Lead. The gap is in `next_appointment_alterations_lead`, the lookup Pipeline uses to display it: it's filtered to only pull from a client's *next* upcoming appointment, and neither of her appointments currently matched that filter — so the field came back empty straight from Airtable, before any code ever touched it. This is not a parsing bug; the Alterations page's own lead field (`most_recent_alterations_lead`) uses a different, unfiltered-in-this-way lookup and was already showing the correct value the whole time. Fix: Pipeline now falls back to `most_recent_alterations_lead` whenever the "next" lookup comes up empty. Separately, to Julia's question: Airtable and Acuity sync one-way only (Acuity → Airtable) — edits made in Airtable never write back to Acuity.
column11:
Issue — Alteration Lead missing from Acuity sync (Zoia Kozakov)
Verified the Acuity data was correct all along — the gap was a lookup field whose filter only pulled from a client's next upcoming appointment, so it came up empty for anyone whose alterations appointments didn't currently match that filter. Fixed by falling back to the same lookup already used successfully elsewhere in the app when the primary one is empty. Also confirmed for Julia: edits in Airtable never sync back to Acuity — it's one-way only. Status: live in Sandbox and Production.
